## How it's built

It's split into two layers. If the code that improves itself could also rewrite its own safety net, one bad edit could break the whole run.

| File | Can Claude edit it? | Role |

ide the project folder. It also gets a fixed list of shell commands (`python`, `pytest`, `pip install`, `ls`, read-only `git`). I left out `--dangerously-skip-permissions` on purpose. If a task needs more, the reflect step will usually note it as a blocker in the journal, and you can add the tool to `TOOLS` in `harness.py`.
- **`pip install` is allowed,** so Claude can install packages into whatever Python environment you start it from. A virtualenv is safer, or remove `pip install` from `TOOLS`.
- **Usage-limit detection** works by matching the error text against a pattern. If Claude Code changes the wording of its limit message, check `logs/supervisor.log` after your first run.
- **Model:** it uses your Claude Code default model. Set `MODEL` in `harness.py` to choose one; if Claude changes it there, the change shows up in git.
- **Licence:** since this is probably a company licence (<company>), it's worth checking whether unattended automated use is fine under your plan or team policy.
